note: The kit pieces both platform panels offer beyond the 37 portable presets, with the same names, types and defaults, so Cavalry and Blender stay in step. Frames are at 30 fps (scaled to the scene); ease is a token in tokens/superside_motion_tokens.json; 'phase' says which of In / Out / Both apply. Each piece animates the selected layers / objects (stagger between them as in the panel) unless 'creates' says it builds new ones. Reference implementations: research/platforms/<tool>/tests/. Pieces with ae_reference copy the After Effects preset exactly (the proof compares the three tools frame by frame); the others are close equivalents.

items.name: Blur In
items.use: Photos, backgrounds, premium moments: sharpens from a soft blur while it fades in
items.ae_reference: SSP 'Blur In': Gaussian Blur 40→0 over Sweep (21 f) on Settle; opacity 0→100 over Glide (9 f), Flat.

items.name: Slam In
items.use: Hero words, titles over footage: big, blurred and turned, it slams into place

items.name: Wipe Reveal
items.use: Bars, lower thirds, underlines: revealed left to right
items.ae_reference: SSP 'Wipe Reveal': Linear Wipe at 90° (hard edge), completion 100→0 over Sweep (21 f) on Cruise: the reveal travels right to left.

items.name: Iris Reveal
items.use: Photo reveals, a new section opening from its centre

items.name: Jello
items.use: Playful accents, stickers: a skew wobble that settles

items.name: Light Speed In
items.use: Fast entrances from the right: slides in leaning, straightens

items.name: Line Draw
items.use: Lines, strokes, underlines (curves / paths only): the stroke draws on

items.name: Chars Rise
items.use: Headlines: letter by letter, each rises and fades in
items.ae_reference: SSP text 'Chars Rise': a Range Selector by characters, shape Ramp Up, Start 0 / End 35 (%), Offset −35→100 over Sweep (21 f) on Cruise; the affected amount a per character = clamp((x − offset)/35) with x its position in % of the text; it moves the character down 50 px, scales it to 118 %, blurs it 14 px and makes it transparent in proportion to a.

items.name: Words Fade Up
items.ae_reference: SSP text 'Words Fade Up': the same Range Selector by words, Offset −35→100 over Stage (33 f) on Settle; 24 px down, blur 8 px, transparent in proportion to a.

items.name: Typewriter
items.use: UI copy, prompts, code: types on letter by letter

items.name: Float
items.use: Products, icons, cards at rest: a slow up and down

items.name: Pulse
items.use: Buttons, live dots, CTAs: a gentle scale beat

items.name: Wiggle
items.use: Hand-made energy on icons and stickers: small random rotation

items.name: Counter
items.use: Numbers that count up to a value (prices, stats)
items.creates: a text layer, or the selected text

items.name: Bars Transition
items.use: A scene change: bars cover the frame, then uncover it
items.creates: bar layers over everything, at the start frame

text_model: Text pieces follow After Effects' Range Selector with a Ramp Up shape: for unit i of n (chars or words) at x_i = 100·(i + 0.5)/n, offset o(t) = −W + (100 + W)·ease(t) over the piece's frames, affected a_i = clamp((x_i − o)/W, 0, 1); then position y += rise·a_i (down on screen), scale = 1 + (scale_from − 1)·a_i, blur = blur_px·a_i, opacity = 1 − a_i. Because a_i is a window of one curve, each unit is baked frame by frame (linear keys at every frame). AE's 'Characters' counts spaces as units (n includes them; a space just has nothing to draw).
